Save the raw HTML of the products route to out.html.
Count the skeleton markers in the saved HTML, which should be 5 for the placeholder rows.

K-020380.example: src/routes/products/+page.server.js returns { products: fetchProducts() } without awaiting, so SvelteKit streams the promise. The curl output contains 5 skeleton-row markers, which means the placeholder rows were sent in the first HTML response.
K-020380.check: grep prints '5' and out.html contains the text 'Loading products'.
traps: curl without -s prints progress noise into the file and may hide the real output.
If you await fetchProducts() in the load, the HTML has no skeleton and grep prints 0.
Run grep on the saved file, not on the terminal output of curl.

steps.do: Install the axe Playwright adapter as a dev dependency.
Create tests/a11y-loading.spec.ts that holds the API response and runs new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze() while the status element is visible.
Assert that the violations array has length 0 and that the contrast ratio of the status text is at least 4.5:1.
Run the accessibility spec.
Confirm the component sets aria-busy on the list container.

K-020381.example: ProductList.svelte sets aria-busy='true' on the ul and a role='status' paragraph with aria-live='polite'. The axe scan runs while the API is held, and the spec asserts violations.length equals 0 and contrast is 4.5:1 or higher.
K-020381.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and grep prints '1'.
traps: Run axe only after the status element is visible, or it scans an empty state.
aria-busy belongs on the list container, not on body.
Axe does not measure text contrast over a skeleton shimmer, so use the solid text color for the check.

steps.do: Build the production bundle.
Start the preview server in a second terminal and keep it running on port 4173.
Run Lighthouse on the products route with the performance category only and save the JSON.
Read the performance score, which must be at least 0.9.
Read first contentful paint in milliseconds, which must be below 1800.

K-020382.example: The products route shows 5 skeleton rows at first paint. The Lighthouse run reports a performance score of 0.93 and first contentful paint of 1412ms.
K-020382.check: jq prints a score of 0.9 or higher and a first-contentful-paint value below 1800.
traps: Lighthouse on the dev server measures unminified code, so run it on the preview build.
A high score does not prove the skeleton appears, so keep the Playwright check too.
Use --chrome-flags=--headless=new, because the old headless flag can fail on newer Chrome.

steps.do: Create tests/products-error.spec.ts that uses page.route('**/api/products') to call route.fulfill with status 500.
Assert that toHaveCount(0) matches '[data-testid=skeleton-row]' and that the text 'Could not load products' is visible.
Run the error spec with the line reporter.
Confirm the error text exists in the route component.
Run svelte-check to confirm the {:catch} block type-checks with no errors.

K-020383.example: The load function in src/routes/products/+page.server.js calls error(500, 'Could not load products') from '@sveltejs/kit' when the fetch fails. The spec returns a 500 from the mock, expects 0 skeleton rows, and expects the error text to be visible.
K-020383.check: Playwright prints '1 passed', grep prints '1', and svelte-check prints '0 errors'.
traps: A fetch that returns 500 does not throw by itself, so check res.ok in the load function.
Leaving the skeleton rendered after an error is a bug, so assert the count is 0.
Do not use 200 with an empty array in the error test, because that tests the empty state instead.

steps.do: Create the composable folder for the new file.
In src/composables/useElementSize.ts, create a ref for width and update it from entry.contentRect.width inside a ResizeObserver started in onMounted.
Call observer.disconnect() inside onUnmounted to stop watching the element.
Run the type checker to confirm the composable compiles.
Run ESLint on the new file to catch unused imports.

K-020384.example: Calling const { width } = useElementSize(chartRef) returns a ref that goes from 0 to 720 when the card is 720px wide. The chart component reads width.value inside a watch, so it redraws only when the number changes.
K-020384.check: npx vue-tsc --noEmit exits with code 0 and prints no errors, and eslint reports 0 problems.
traps: Reading the width once in setup gives 0 because the element is not mounted yet.
Forgetting disconnect leaks observers after the chart unmounts.
Using the window resize event misses size changes from a sidebar toggle.

steps.do: Install the ECharts library into the project.
In LineChart.vue, call echarts.init on the template ref inside onMounted.
Watch the width ref and call chart.resize() when it changes.
Call chart.dispose() in onBeforeUnmount to free canvas memory.
Run the Vitest suite for the chart component.

K-020385.example: When the container shrinks from 960px to 480px, watch(width, () => chart?.resize()) fires once and the canvas redraws at 480px wide. The component keeps a single chart instance and never calls init a second time.
K-020385.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 1 passed' and the resize test asserts that resize was called exactly once.
traps: Calling echarts.init on every update creates duplicate canvases.
Skipping dispose leaves stale instances in memory.
Calling resize without a null check on chart throws when the test runs before mount.

steps.do: Create the SparkLine component file.
Set the root svg to a viewBox of 0 0 300 100, width 100% and height auto in a scoped style block.
Use v-for over the values prop to build a computed points string for a polyline.
Give the svg role img and an aria-label so screen readers announce the chart summary.
Run the axe accessibility scanner against a page that mounts the component.

K-020386.example: A 300 by 100 viewBox with width 100% draws the same proportions at 150px or 600px. The polyline points are computed by scaling props.values into the 100 unit viewBox height.
K-020386.check: The axe CLI reports 0 violations for http://localhost:5173/spark.
traps: Setting a fixed pixel width breaks the viewBox scaling.
Leaving out role img leaves the chart unlabelled for assistive tech.
Swapping x and y when scaling produces a flipped line.

steps.do: Create a computed named visibleData that keeps every Nth point, where N is Math.ceil of pointCount divided by maxPoints.
Set maxPoints to 60 when width is below 640 and to 240 otherwise.
Pass visibleData into the series data of the chart option instead of the raw prop.
Run the Vitest unit test for the sampling function.
Run Lighthouse on the page and confirm the performance score is at least 90.

K-020387.example: A prop with 1440 points on a 390px screen is reduced to 60 points, which means keeping every 24th point. The computed visibleData updates automatically when the width ref crosses 640.
K-020387.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 3 passed' and Lighthouse reports a performance score of 90 or higher.
traps: Sampling the raw prop instead of the computed loses the reactive update on resize.
Dropping the last point hides the most recent value.
Using Math.floor instead of Math.ceil can produce 63 points when the limit is 60.

steps.do: Search table components for header cell markup.
Count the header cells per file so you know the total label count.
Search for hardcoded empty-state and pagination strings.
Search for aria-label and sr-only text, since those strings are also translatable.
Create the planning file that will hold one key candidate per string.
Write each found string into i18n-table-strings.md, one key candidate per line.
Run the existing table tests to record the baseline before any change.

K-020388.example: rg -c '<th' src/components prints src/components/UsersTable.tsx:6, so the plan lists 6 keys under table.users.columns. The sr-only text 'Sort by name' is a seventh string and goes on the list too.
K-020388.check: rg -c prints a nonzero count for each table file, and i18n-table-strings.md lists the same number of header keys plus every aria-label or sr-only string. npx playwright test tests/table.spec.ts exits 0 and reports its baseline pass count.
traps: Small models miss strings in aria-label and sr-only text. Count those too.
Do not count className values as visible text.

steps.do: List numeric fields in the table data type files.
Check which numeric cells already use right alignment or tabular digits.
Plan each numeric column to use tabular-nums and text-end. Confirm the current classes first.
Check whether formatting already uses Intl.NumberFormat or Intl.DateTimeFormat.
Find existing toLocaleString calls and hardcoded currency symbols that the plan must replace.
Count the toLocaleString calls that must be replaced. The target after the change is zero.
Find the supported locales so you can record them.
Create the supported-locales file, then write one locale per line.
Run the formatting test that covers the currency and number output.

K-020389.example: rg -n 'toLocaleString' src prints src/components/InvoiceTable.tsx:42, and the plan replaces it with new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }).format(total). The amount cell then uses tabular-nums text-end so the digits line up in every locale.
K-020389.check: rg -n prints each hardcoded currency or toLocaleString hit with file and line. rg -c 'toLocaleString' src prints the count the plan must reduce to 0. supported-locales.txt has one locale per line, and the plan lists one formatter per numeric column type. npx playwright test tests/invoice-format.spe…
traps: Small models hardcode the currency symbol in the cell instead of passing the currency code.
Do not format dates by splitting strings. Use Intl.DateTimeFormat.

steps.do: Check where the dir attribute is set in the app shell.
Find the root html element or layout file that will own the dir attribute.
Check whether the app already sets document direction in code.
List icons in table headers that point in a direction, such as sort arrows.
Check which icons already use rtl: classes.
Plan rtl:rotate-180 on directional icons only. Leave non-directional icons such as checkmarks unchanged.
Count the directional icons that will receive rtl:rotate-180. The count must match the list in the plan.
Run the RTL table test that checks icon direction in Arabic.

K-020390.example: rg -n 'dir=' index.html prints no match, so the plan sets dir from the locale in the root layout. The ChevronRight icon in the sort button gets rtl:rotate-180 so it points the correct way in Arabic.
K-020390.check: rg -n 'dir=' src shows one match on the root html or layout element and none on each table. rg -c 'rtl:rotate-180' src/components prints a count equal to the number of directional icons in the plan. npx playwright test tests/rtl-table.spec.ts exits 0.
traps: Small models set dir on each table instead of the root element.
Do not mirror icons that have no direction, such as a checkmark.

steps.do: Declare the breakpoint as a plain const 640 in the component script.
Compute legendPosition with a computed that returns 'bottom' when width is below 640 and 'right' otherwise.
Bind legendPosition into the legend.orient or legend.bottom field of the chart option object.
Run the Playwright spec on the mobile project at a 390px viewport.
Assert in that spec that the legend top edge is below the plot bottom edge.

K-020391.example: At width 390 the computed returns 'bottom' and the legend renders under the x-axis. At width 1024 it returns 'right' and the legend sits beside the plot.
K-020391.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' for the mobile project and the spec asserts legend y position is greater than the plot bottom edge.
traps: Using a ref for the breakpoint instead of a plain const adds needless reactivity.
Comparing against the string '640' instead of the number 640 gives wrong results.
Testing only at desktop width misses the mobile layout entirely.

steps.do: Add a frameId variable and cancel any pending frame with cancelAnimationFrame at the start of the observer callback.
Schedule chart.resize inside requestAnimationFrame so it runs at most once per frame.
Cancel the pending frame with cancelAnimationFrame in onBeforeUnmount.
Run the Playwright spec that drags the window width and counts resize calls.
Assert in that spec that the resize count is at most 13 during a 200ms drag at 60fps.

K-020392.example: A 200ms drag from 800px to 400px produces about 60 observer callbacks but only about 12 chart.resize calls, one per frame. The spec counts the calls and asserts the total is at most 13.
K-020392.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the counter stays at or below 13 for the drag.
traps: Calling cancelAnimationFrame with a stale id does nothing useful.
Skipping cleanup in onBeforeUnmount lets a frame fire after the chart is gone.
Using setTimeout with 0 delay does not line up with the paint cycle.

steps.do: Start the local static server on port 8080 from the project root.
Run axe on the Arabic onboarding page and fail on any WCAG 2 AA violation.
Repeat the axe run for the German page, since its longer words often lower contrast in buttons.
Confirm the output has no color-contrast rule and the command exits with status 0.

K-020393.example: Text color #767676 on white gives 4.54:1, which passes, while #8a8a8a gives 3.4:1 and fails the 4.5:1 rule. A failing button in the German page shows color-contrast in the axe output.
K-020393.check: Each axe command exits with status 0, and its output contains no color-contrast violation.
traps: Checking only the English page misses contrast loss from translated colors on buttons or hints.
Using --tags wcag2aa skips some AAA rules, so do not claim the page meets AAA.
Setting the server to a different port makes the axe URL return a connection error, which is not a pass.

steps.do: Run the overflow spec, which loads each locale at a 320px viewport and fails if scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth.
Count the root font-size rule to confirm text scales in rem, not px.
Confirm the Playwright output reports every locale passed with no horizontal scrollbar.

K-020394.example: A German heading at 320px wide wraps onto three lines instead of pushing the Next button off screen. The spec asserts scrollWidth <= clientWidth for each of the 4 locales.
K-020394.check: Playwright prints '4 passed' and grep -c prints at least 1.
traps: Testing only at 1280px hides overflow that appears on phones.
Fixed px widths on the step container cause clipping when translated text is about 30 percent longer.
A passing test on short English strings does not prove German strings fit.

steps.do: Confirm the Japanese onboarding file is UTF-8 encoded.
Check that the page declares a UTF-8 charset in its head.
Run the Intl formatting test, which checks that the step count and date formatting match each locale's expected output.
Confirm the Node test exits with status 0 and prints each locale's formatted number.

K-020395.example: file prints 'UTF-8 text' for ja/index.html. The Node test expects new Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG').format(3) to print the Arabic-Indic digit three, and the test fails if it prints the Latin 3.
K-020395.check: file reports UTF-8 text, grep -ci utf-8 prints at least 1, and node exits with status 0 after printing all locale checks.
traps: Saving a file as Shift_JIS or Windows-1252 garbles Japanese or Arabic even when the page looks correct in your editor.
Hardcoding digits in the HTML bypasses Intl, so a locale shows Latin numerals when it should show local ones.
A missing meta charset tag lets browsers guess the encoding, which can break on some systems.

steps.do: Search the project for existing accessibility modifiers.
Decide that the loading message is announced to VoiceOver as it changes.
Make the optional dismiss button at least 44 by 44 points.
Require text contrast of at least 4.5:1 against the toast background.
Write each rule as a numbered line in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
Confirm the rules file exists.

K-020396.example: The loading view gets .accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently), and the success message calls AccessibilityNotification.Announcement('Saved').post(). The dismiss button uses .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).
K-020396.check: ls prints ACCESSIBILITY.md, and the file lists 44 points and 4.5:1 as numbers.
traps: Small models pick a 36 point button, which is under the 44 point target.
They rely on color alone to show success or failure.
They use UIKit calls such as UIAccessibility.post instead of the SwiftUI notification.

steps.do: List existing test files.
Plan three unit tests: idle to loading, loading to success, and the 300ms minimum honored.
Plan one snapshot per state: idle, loading, success, failure, which is four snapshots.
Confirm the Toast scheme exists for the test run.
Cap each test at 1 second so a hang fails fast.

K-020397.example: testMinimumTimeHonored asserts the toast is still visible at 299ms and hidden at 301ms, using a clock that advances a fixed Duration. Four snapshots cover the four ToastState cases.
K-020397.check: xcodebuild -list prints a Schemes: section that includes Toast.
traps: Small models make tests sleep for the real 300 milliseconds, which slows the suite.
They skip the failure snapshot.
They skip the scheme check and then fail with a missing scheme error.

steps.do: Write the numeric targets: text contrast 4.5:1, focus indicator contrast 3:1, minimum target size 24px, and 44px as the goal.
List the existing color tokens in the style files.
List the style files that contain button rules.
Check that axe-core is installed so contrast can be measured later.

K-020398.example: The plan sets text contrast at 4.5:1 and focus contrast at 3:1, and grep finds --color-primary and --color-danger tokens. npm ls prints axe-core with its installed version.
K-020398.check: The grep prints each color token, and npm ls prints a version number for axe-core.
traps: Using 3:1 for body text, when body text needs 4.5:1 unless it is 18pt or larger.
Setting a target size with no measurement, such as making it bigger without a 24px or 44px number.

steps.do: Find existing toggle buttons by searching for the word toggle in Vue files.
Decide that the component exposes the on and off state with a boolean defineModel named pressed.
Decide that the button binds aria-pressed to that model and keeps the label text the same in both states.
Check that the installed Vue version supports defineModel, which needs Vue 3.4 or newer.

K-020399.example: The grep finds 2 toggle files, and the plan binds aria-pressed to the pressed model with the label Mute unchanged. npm ls prints vue at 3.4.21 or higher, so defineModel is available.
K-020399.check: The grep lists the toggle files, and npm ls prints a Vue version of 3.4 or higher.
traps: Changing the label to Muted or Unmuted, which repeats the state that aria-pressed already announces.
Using aria-checked on a button, which is the wrong attribute for a toggle button.

steps.do: Check package.json for an accessibility lint plugin.
Check for a Playwright config file for browser-based accessibility checks.
Set the pass rule as zero serious or critical axe violations on the button test page.
Set the lint rule as zero errors from the Vue accessibility lint plugin on AppButton.vue.
Run the linter once to record a baseline count of problems.

K-020400.example: The grep finds eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility in package.json, and the eslint run reports a baseline of 3 problems. The plan sets the gate to 0 serious or critical axe violations and 0 lint errors.
K-020400.check: The grep prints the plugin line from package.json, and eslint prints a problem count that is recorded in the plan.
traps: Setting the gate without a baseline, so the team cannot tell new problems from old ones.
Counting warnings as passes when the rule is zero errors.

steps.do: Count the margin-left or margin-right rules left in the onboarding stylesheet. Expect 0.
Count the text-align rules that still use left. Expect 0.
Run the Playwright spec that loads the Arabic page and checks document direction and step order. Expect 1 passed.
Count the spec's assertions on the html dir attribute. Expect 1.

K-020401.example: The first grep should print 0 after replacing margin-left with margin-inline-start and margin-right with margin-inline-end. The second should print 0 after replacing text-align: left with text-align: start. The Playwright spec opens http://localhost:8080/onboarding/ar/ and asserts document.documentElement.dir equals rtl.
K-020401.check: The two greps print 0, Playwright prints '1 passed' with the RTL assertions green, and the last grep prints 1.
traps: Using text-align: left in CSS keeps Arabic text aligned to the wrong edge.
Mirroring icons by hand is error-prone; test the actual rendered positions, not the source.
Quote the grep -E pattern in one argument, or the shell may split it and the count can read 0 for the wrong reason.

steps.do: Find every button tag in src so you can check which ones show only an icon.
List each button with the lines after it so you can see which ones hold only an SVG icon.
Count the icon-only buttons and write their file paths into the plan.
Count the aria-label attributes already in src so you know how many names exist before the change.
Read the current component to see where the new label prop belongs.
Run axe against the dev server on port 5173 and record the number of button-name violations it reports.

K-020402.example: The search finds 9 buttons, and 3 render only an SVG icon, so the plan requires label Close dialog on each. Each label must be a short action name, not an icon name like X. axe reports 3 button-name violations before the change.
K-020402.check: axe prints a button-name violation count that matches your icon-only count, and that count falls to 0 once the labels are added.
traps: Using title instead of aria-label, which many screen readers announce unreliably.
Repeating visible words in the label, which makes the name redundant for screen reader users.

steps.do: List every use of the disabled attribute in Vue templates.
Count the disabled uses per file and sum the counts. The sum must equal the match count from the previous step.
Decide that a loading state uses aria-disabled set to true and stays focusable, because native disabled removes the button from focus order.
Decide that a loading state sets aria-busy to true and keeps the label visible.
Open PLAN-button-a11y.md and confirm both decisions appear in it.
Run axe on the settings page and record the number of color-contrast violations for the Saving label at the 4.5:1 minimum.
After the change, list every aria-disabled attribute and confirm no element also has the disabled attribute.

K-020403.example: The search finds 6 disabled attributes, and the plan changes the save button to aria-disabled=true while busy so its focus stays put. The label still reads Saving and aria-busy is set to true. axe reports 0 color-contrast violations for that label.
K-020403.check: The per-file sum equals the total from the first search, cat shows both decisions in the plan, and axe reports 0 color-contrast violations at 4.5:1.
traps: Adding disabled and aria-disabled together, which gives mixed signals about the state.
Replacing the label with a spinner only, which removes the accessible name during loading.

steps.do: List every Color value already defined so the plan reuses existing tokens.
Check whether a token file already exists before adding a new pair.
Record each planned pair as foreground Color::Rgb and background Color::Rgb with its computed contrast ratio.
Mark any pair below 4.5:1 as rejected and pick a darker or lighter background for it.

K-020404.example: White text Color::Rgb(255,255,255) on background Color::Rgb(37,99,235) gives about 5.2:1, so the pair is accepted. The same white text on Color::Rgb(96,165,250) gives about 2.5:1, so that pair is rejected.
K-020404.check: Every row in docs/button-tokens.md shows a ratio of 4.5 or higher, or is marked rejected.
traps: Small models compare RGB distance instead of WCAG relative luminance, which gives wrong results; use the luminance formula.
Color::Rgb needs a truecolor terminal, so the plan must also name an Indexed fallback.
Do not write hex strings such as #2563eb into ratatui code; the API takes numbers.

steps.do: Find existing Padding and border settings so the plan matches them.
Confirm the source directory layout before naming new files.
Write the spacing tokens as cell counts: height 3 rows, horizontal padding 1 cell per side, minimum width 12 cells.
Count the planned width for the longest label and confirm it fits the minimum width rule.

K-020405.example: An 8-character label with a 1-cell padding on each side and a 1-cell border on each side needs 12 cells, which equals the minimum. A 3-row button is one top border row, one text row, and one bottom border row.
K-020405.check: rg -c "Padding" src prints a count and the plan states height 3, padding 1, and minimum width 12 in cells.
traps: Small models write rem, px, or em; terminals have no such units, so use cell counts only.
Forgetting the 2 border cells makes the label width calculation wrong by 2.
Do not plan a 2-row button with a border, because the bordered block needs at least 3 rows.

steps.do: Check whether the project already depends on unicode-width for measuring display columns.
Find existing button label strings so the plan can compare their lengths.
Write the label rule: Title Case, at most 16 display columns, with ellipsis truncation past that limit.
Run the existing test suite to confirm the baseline passes before any label change.

K-020406.example: The label Save changes is 12 columns and fits the 16-column budget, while Export all customer records is 28 columns and gets truncated to 15 columns plus an ellipsis. The plan records the 16-column limit in docs/button-tokens.md.
K-020406.check: cargo test ends with test result: ok and the plan states a limit of 16 display columns.
traps: Small models count bytes or characters with len(), but wide CJK characters take 2 columns, so measure display width instead.
Do not plan truncation without an ellipsis rule, because a cut label looks like a complete word.
If unicode-width is missing, record it as a build-stage dependency; do not assume it is present.

steps.do: List every text-gray-400 or text-gray-300 use, since these fail on white.
Record the planned replacement: text-gray-600 on bg-white gives about 7.6:1, which passes.
Record text-gray-500 on bg-white at about 4.8:1 as the minimum allowed value for body copy.
Check the Tailwind config for any custom gray that overrides the defaults.
Count planned classes that use opacity utilities, since opacity can drop contrast below 4.5:1.

K-020407.example: text-gray-400 on bg-white is about 2.5:1 and fails, so replace it with text-gray-600, which is about 7.6:1. Keep the heading in text-gray-900.
K-020407.check: rg -n -F text-gray-400 prints the lines to replace, and the plan lists a ratio of 4.5:1 or higher for every text token.
traps: Small models assume gray-400 is readable because it looks light; compute the ratio instead of guessing. Tailwind v4 may define colors in CSS @theme inside app.css rather than tailwind.config.js, so c…

steps.do: Find existing live regions so you do not duplicate one.
Plan a container with role status and aria-live polite that is rendered on mount, even when the list is empty.
Plan the announcement text to appear within 200ms after the list updates.
Count list components that fetch data, since each one needs this region.
Record the count in the plan file so the build stage knows the target.

K-020408.example: Plan one role status container in ProductList.tsx that is always in the DOM and announces 'No products match your filters' within 200ms. Use aria-live polite, not assertive, because an empty result is not an emergency.
K-020408.check: rg -l -F useQuery src lists each fetching component, and grep -c prints a count that matches the rows in the plan file.
traps: A live region inserted only when the list is empty is often not announced, because screen readers need the container present before the change. Small models also set aria-live assertive by default, w…

steps.do: Find existing small buttons that use h-8 sizing.
Plan min-h-11 (2.75rem, which is 44px at the default 16px root) and min-w-11 for width.
Plan inline-flex items-center on the button so the label stays centered at 44px.
Count buttons that already use min-h-11 so you can reuse the pattern.
Write the chosen size into the plan file.

K-020409.example: Plan the CTA as 'inline-flex min-h-11 min-w-11 items-center rounded-md px-4' so it is 44px tall. Reject min-h-10 because it is 40px.
K-020409.check: rg -c -F min-h-11 src prints a count, and grep -c 44px docs/empty-state-plan.md prints 1 or more after the size is written.
traps: Small models pick min-h-10 (40px) and call it 44px; min-h-11 is the 44px step. Padding alone does not guarantee the target size, so set min-h explicitly.

steps.do: Count svg elements in the components to see which may need hiding.
Count icons already marked aria-hidden, which tells you the existing convention.
Plan aria-hidden true and focusable false on each decorative svg.
Find components that already handle reduced motion.
Plan motion-reduce:animate-none on any animated icon and cap the entry animation at 300ms.

K-020410.example: The illustration svg gets aria-hidden='true' and focusable='false', and the icon uses 'animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none'. The entry transition stays under 300ms.
K-020410.check: rg -c -F svg src/components and rg -c -F aria-hidden src/components give counts, and every decorative svg in the plan appears in the aria-hidden count.
traps: Tailwind's animate-bounce and animate-spin loop forever, so motion-reduce:animate-none is required. Small models also add alt text to decorative svgs, which makes screen readers announce them.

steps.do: Write a test that mounts LoadingInput with props loading set to true, using mount from @vue/test-utils.
Assert that the native input element has the disabled attribute, not just that the loading prop is true.
Confirm the spec file has both a loading true case and a loading false case.
Run the spec file with Vitest in run mode.

K-020411.example: mount(LoadingInput, { props: { loading: true } }) followed by expect(wrapper.find('input').attributes('disabled')).toBeDefined() should pass. Then call wrapper.setProps({ loading: false }) and expect the disabled attribute to be undefined.
K-020411.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 2 passed (2)' and grep lists both the true and false assertions.
traps: Small models check the component prop instead of the rendered input attribute, so the test passes even when the DOM is wrong.
Skipping the reset to loading false leaves the input stuck disabled in real use and the test does not catch it.
Reading wrapper.vm.loading checks internal state, not what the user sees.

steps.do: Mount LoadingInput with loading true and count elements matching the spinner class.
Assert the count is exactly 1 when loading is true.
Use setProps to set loading to false and assert the count is exactly 0.
Run the spec file to execute both assertions.
